spec.title: Bound the unbounded verdict fields and de-rot the phase list in status.schema.json
spec.problem: Two defects in plugins/pipeline/schemas/status.schema.json, a file that is committed to git and archived verbatim by the Librarian. (1) #34: events[].verdict is a bare {"type": "string"} with no bound, so any prose an agent writes lands in a public tree at full length. The same is true of flags[].verdict, which #34 does not name even though it is the same field, in the same file, under the same archival mechanism, and which in the committed corpus carries the LONGEST observed verdict of the two. (2) #42: the current_phase description's hand-maintained example list has rotted -- verified, it blesses two literals commands/pipeline.md never writes and omits six it does. A material fact that governs both fixes and that neither issue states: status.schema.json appears in NO AGENT_RULES entry in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, and that walker does not implement maxLength or pattern at all. The file's ONLY runtime reader is voice-lint.mjs, which reads exactly one key out of it (properties.current_phase.pattern). So a maxLength added here refuses nothing on its own; #34's stated precedent (flags[].summary's maxLength: 140) is likewise unenforced, and is honored in practice only because pipeline.md restates it as a writer rule. The fix must therefore either come with a reader or be labelled as documented intent, not shipped as a guard that does not guard.
spec.root_cause: status.schema.json is a documentation contract with a single partial reader. Both defects are the same underlying condition: a constraint written into this file is not read by anything, so it can be wrong (the phase list) or absent (the verdict bound) indefinitely without any check going red. #42 is the fourth member of the 'hand-maintained phase vocabulary rots' class named in #39's spec; #34 is the field that #30 simultaneously promoted to load-bearing (pipeline-telemetry.mjs's docstring makes verdict the tell that fixes the meaning of a stored measurement) and left unbounded.
requirements: R2. flags.items.properties.verdict gains the SAME maxLength: 32. Ruling on the owner's scope question: FOLD IN, do not defer. It is the same field name, the same file, the same commit-and-archive-verbatim mechanism, and #34's argument applies to it word for word. It is also the field carrying the longest verdict actually observed in the corpus (18 chars, vs 15 for events[]), so deferring would leave the larger of the two values unbounded. A deferral would have to be written as an issue that is #34 with one identifier changed, to produce a second one-line diff to a line eight lines away from this one.

R3. The current_phase description's example list is corrected to the literals commands/pipeline.md actually writes, PLUS halted-error, and the <phase>-error family is named as a shape rather than omitted. halted-error is the trap: pipeline.md never writes it, so a mechanical derivation from pipeline.md alone DELETES it -- but the schema's own pattern alternates it explicitly (^([0-5](\.5)?-[a-z0-9-]+|halted-error)$) and gate-phase-entry.mjs:241 returns true for it by name. Removing it would refuse correct work.

R4. A corpus-conformance check asserts every committed events[].verdict and flags[].verdict conforms to the cap, reading the cap FROM the schema rather than from a copied literal, and preceded by a vacuity control asserting the corpus is non-empty and of the expected shape. Without this, the cap is a comment; with a copied literal, the check and the schema drift.

R5. The three test comments that cite the schema:13 rot as LIVE present-tense evidence are re-anchored, because R3 makes all three false on landing. They are plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh:13-14, plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh:511-512, and plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh:711. The negative-control INPUT '3-scope-drift-adjudication' at test-gate-phase-entry.sh:514 stays valid (pipeline.md still never writes it); only the justification prose dies, and it must be restated in the past tense naming #42.

R6. The description of each capped field states plainly that nothing validates status.json against this schema, so a later reader does not mistake the cap for an enforced control and skip writing the enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: AC1. plugins/pipeline/schemas/status.schema.json parses as JSON, and both events.items.properties.verdict and flags.items.properties.verdict carry maxLength: 32 with type still "string".

AC2. VACUITY CONTROL, asserted BEFORE any property is asserted over the corpus: the walk over .pipeline/*/status.json finds at least 6 committed records, every one of them parses, and every one has events as an array. The floor is a derived >= that can only grow, in the idiom already used at test-gate-phase-entry.sh AC19 ('the corpus walk found at least 4 committed records'). If the walk returns zero the check must FAIL, never pass green.

AC3. Every events[].verdict and flags[].verdict string in the committed corpus has length <= the cap. NON-ZERO CONTROL, required, not optional: with the schema's cap temporarily set to 17 the check must go RED and must name .pipeline/17/status.json's flags[] entry 'APPROVE_WITH_NOTES' (18 chars) as the violator. A check that has never been watched to fail on this corpus has not been shown to read it.

AC4. The check reads the cap from status.schema.json, not from a literal in the test. Proven by mutating ONLY the schema's maxLength value and observing the check's verdict change; a test carrying its own copy of 32 passes AC3 and fails this one.

AC5. The corrected description names exactly the set derivable from commands/pipeline.md by grep -o '"\?current_phase"\?: *"[^"]*"' , plus halted-error, less the <phase>-error template. Asserted as SET EQUALITY in both directions, not as a substring grep -- voice-lint.mjs's first phase table is the recorded precedent for why a substring grep is insufficient (a phase named in a comment satisfies it).

AC6. halted-error is STILL named in the description after the fix. This is R3's negative control and it is the criterion most likely to be silently violated, because the obvious mechanical fix removes it: pipeline.md writes it nowhere, yet gate-phase-entry.mjs:241 is `if (phase === "halted-error") return true;` and the schema's own pattern alternates it.
AC7. Neither 3-impl-verification-unverified nor 3-scope-drift-adjudication appears anywhere in status.schema.json after the fix.

AC8. UNCHANGED CONSUMER: properties.current_phase.pattern is byte-identical before and after. voice-lint.mjs:224 reads exactly this one key out of this file and nothing else; the fix touches the sibling description key and must not perturb it.

AC9. UNCHANGED CONSUMER, behavioural: plugins/pipeline/tests/test-voice-lint.sh is green after the change, AND one non-zero control is run -- feed voice-lint a malformed current_phase and confirm it still emits the failure naming status.schema.json (test-voice-lint.sh:191 asserts that string). Green alone does not distinguish 'still works' from 'went silent', which is the exact failure voice-lint.mjs's own docstring warns about.

AC10. No file under plugins/pipeline/tests/ asserts in the PRESENT tense that status.schema.json's description blesses a phase pipeline.md never writes. Checkable by grep over the three sites named in R5; each must read as history referencing #42, not as a live claim.

AC11. plugins/pipeline/tests/run.sh is green AND the total assertion count is >= the count at the pre-change commit, recorded in impl-report.json as two numbers with the platform each was measured on. Per #47, a suite can lose assertions silently while still reporting failed=0, and per #33 a floor that is not re-derived decays.
out_of_scope: Adding maxLength or pattern support to validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's schema walker. Its header says these are advisory deliberately, and implementing them would change the validation behaviour of EVERY schema at once -- a far larger and differently-tiered change than two lines in one file. The bespoke groundOpenQuestions check at validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:538 is the established precedent for handling one field's constraint outside the walker.

Registering status.json in AGENT_RULES so it gets validated at all. This is a real gap (voice-lint.mjs:238 states it outright: 'Nothing else validates this file') but it is a new enforcement surface with its own fail-open/fail-closed design questions, not a schema annotation. If the owner wants it, it is its own issue.
Converting events[].verdict or flags[].verdict to an enum. SecOps already ruled against this in #34 and the reasoning is recorded there; not re-litigated.
events[].phase, which #34 explicitly excludes because #30 closed the key-forming risk at pipeline-telemetry.mjs:181.
Changing properties.current_phase.pattern. Only the sibling description key is edited.

Making the phase example list machine-derived at build time. #42 says outright the description is prose with no requirement to be machine-checked; AC5 checks it once, at this edit. A generator is a different change.

Add one bogus literal (e.g. 9-not-a-phase) to the description list, then separately DELETE one real literal (e.g. 3-impl-complete). Both must redden. Two mutations because set equality has two directions and a one-directional check (subset, or a substring grep) catches only the first -- voice-lint.mjs's original phase table failed exactly this way.

Remove halted-error from the description. Must redden. This is the mutation the naive fix actually performs, so it is the one most likely to survive an author who derived the list from pipeline.md and never looked at gate-phase-entry.mjs:241.

Re-insert 3-scope-drift-adjudication into the description. Must redden. Change one character inside properties.current_phase.pattern (e.g. [0-5] -> [0-6]). Must redden. Asserting on the pattern's VALUE, not on its presence: a presence check survives any edit to the regex, which is the reader voice-lint.mjs actually consumes.

Feed voice-lint a current_phase of '99-nonsense' and require the failure string naming status.schema.json. Then, as the control on the control, feed it a well-formed phase and require SILENCE. One direction alone cannot tell a working check from one that fires on everything.

Delete one assertion from any touched suite and confirm the recorded count drops below the pre-change figure. The two counts must be measured on the SAME platform: per #47 there is a real 32-assertion macOS/ubuntu gap at one commit, so comparing a local post-change count against a CI pre-change count measures the runner, not the change.

expected_survivor.criterion: AC3, under the mutation 'raise the schema cap from 32 to 64'
expected_survivor.why_it_survives: It genuinely should survive. The corpus maximum is 18, so every value conforms to 32 and to 64 alike; no committed record can distinguish them. Kept deliberately as the harness's own non-zero control, per evidence.md: a battery in which every mutation reddens cannot tell coverage from a rubber stamp. It also states the honest limit of this criterion out loud -- AC3 constrains the cap from BELOW (via the 17 control) and not from above, so the choice between 32 and 64 rests on the refusal argument in q2, not on the corpus. Anyone who reports this mutation as CAUGHT has a harness bug, not a better test.

open_questions.question: The cap will not actually stop anything on its own -- nothing in the pipeline validates status.json against this schema. Should we ship the cap plus a small test that checks the committed records against it, or just write the cap down as documented intent?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether AC3 exists at all. Schema-only means the one acceptance criterion that would prove the cap works cannot be written, because nothing refuses anything -- and a criterion that cannot fail is the defect this project files issues about. Adding the corpus check makes the schema a thing the repo reads, at the cost of one new test file.

options.label: Schema + a writer rule in pipeline.md

open_questions.question: How long should a verdict be allowed to be -- 32 characters, or 64?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It changes what the cap refuses. The longest verdict that exists anywhere -- declared or observed -- is APPROVE_WITH_NOTES at 18 characters. At 32 the cap refuses a run-on sentence written into the field by mistake; at 64 it refuses only a paragraph, and a short editorial sentence like 'approved with some minor concerns noted' (39 chars) sails through.

options.label: 32 (recommended)
options.implication: 1.78x the largest real value. Leaves room for any plausible new token; refuses free-text. Refuses no correct work I can construct -- every declared verdict across all four artifact schemas is <= 18.

3.6x. Safer against an unusually long future verdict, but stops catching the realistic mistake, which is a sentence rather than a token. evidence.md's corollary applies: a bound with large headroom never fires on a realistic mistake.

options.label: 18 (exactly the observed and declared maximum)
options.implication: Rejected. It refuses the next legitimate verdict at the moment someone records it -- which is #34's own argument against an enum, reappearing as a too-tight cap. A 19-char verdict is not a defect.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: 32. It is derived rather than round: 18 from the declared closed vocabulary (corroborated by the corpus maximum of 18) plus headroom sized to admit any longer SCREAMING_SNAKE token while sitting under the length of a sentence. On the owner's question of whether 6 committed records are enough to derive from -- they are not, on their own, and I have not relied on them for the bound. The bound comes from the DECLARED enums in the four artifact schemas, which are a closed set rather than a sample; the corpus only confirms that nothing in the wild exceeds it. That distinction is what makes 32 defensible from a small corpus.

A cap of 17 or below WOULD have invalidated a committed record (.pipeline/17/status.json's APPROVE_WITH_NOTES) -- that is a real floor, not a hypothetical, and it is AC3's non-zero control. AC6 is the control on that. edge_cases_covered: Zero committed records: the walk reports files=0 and the vacuity predicate REFUSES that count rather than passing green.
A record whose JSON does not parse: NAMED in `unreadable`, and read < files so the shortfall is visible; the well-formed sibling is asserted NOT to be named.
A record whose events is an object rather than an array: reported on the shape conjunct, which is mutated apart from the count conjunct.
An ABSENT verdict key: schema-valid, not a violation, and not counted -- so the cap cannot become a requirement (one live record depends on this).
A verdict exactly at the cap vs one character over: the over-long fixtures are built as cap+1 characters, derived from the schema value.

Both fields independently: an over-long events[].verdict and an over-long flags[].verdict are separate crafted records, because at cap 17 the events[] branch sits in the passing cell of the conjunction and is never exercised.

The reporting instrument itself: an absent report reads <no-report>, a present report missing the key reads <no-field:KEY>, and a present key with an empty list reads empty -- so 'nothing wrong' and 'nothing measured' are distinguishable.
Set equality in both directions with a control per direction, over a vacuity floor on BOTH sets (two empty sets are equal).
The pattern accepts every literal the description names, asserted over the whole set rather than a representative member, with a control that the same pattern refuses a malformed phase.
AC10's grep is proven against the ACTUAL pre-change wording of all three sites, one cell each, plus a negative cell on the sentence that legitimately survives.
